title: review: fix round 1 (review): S2d1 cache-aware context router in shadow: cacheability, effective cache cost and a cache-
spec: Fix round 1 for T-1257: review T-1263 requested changes. fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/context_router.py:152 [high]: The downgrade eligibility test is `reason == "ambiguous"`, which inverts rule (e). `ambiguous` is a named-rule reason and must be exempt. Only generic fallback reasons (the source_type fallback strings from _choice) are eligible. In active mode, ambiguous dynamic LONG items get downgraded while the eligible fallback items never do. Shadow rows and the cache-shadow share are computed on the wrong p fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/spawn.py:1410 [med]: provider="claude" is passed only in the run_worker review and fallback-execute paths. The Codex dispatch path never passes provider="codex", and scout passes none. Codex-executed tasks therefore log cache_cost None and cache_data 'missing', and the Codex write_ratio is never used. fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/cli.py:694 [low]: The --cache-shadow summary reads decision_log with `a.root or scorecard.STATE`, while the context card uses scorecard.STATE, so the two can describe different data. The presented level is parsed from the candidates suffix. Under active cache_mode that suffix is already the adjusted level, so changed_share reads 0 even when adjustments were applied. fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/cache_telemetry.py:40 [low]: dynamic_cost indexes ratios[f"{provider}_write_ratio"] directly, so an unexpected provider string raises KeyError. route() is meant never to raise for configuration, and this would break the shadow row for that call. fix round 1 rule: Eligibility: only the generic source_type fallback reason strings are eligible for downgrade; 'ambiguous' and every other named-rule reason are exempt (invert the current test, add a test with an ambiguous dynamic LONG item untouched and a fallback dynamic LONG item downgraded). Pass provider='codex' on the Codex dispatch path in daemon/spawn and provider='claude' for scout and the other Claude roles so no Codex run logs cache_data missing. In the --cache-shadow summary use the same root as the context card and read the presented level from the deterministic map (cache_adjusted_level versus the level stored before adjustment, stored explicitly on the row as presented_level), not from the candidates suffix. dynamic_cost returns None for an unknown provider string instead of raising. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0; do not ask questions; report files changed and failures-only output.
acceptance: tests/test_context_router.py::test_cache_fields_on_rows_and_presented_level_unchanged_in_shadow (route() levels identical with cache_mode shadow and with no cache_mode key; deterministic maps present)
tests/test_context_router.py::test_cache_adjusted_level_algorithm (downgrade only for eligible dynamic items; named-rule reasons untouched; HIDE untouched; provider None gives cache_cost None)

fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/context_router.py:152 [high]: The downgrade eligibility test is `reason == "ambiguous"`, which inverts rule (e). `ambiguous` is a named-rule reason and must be exempt. Only generic fallback reasons (the source_type fallback strings from _choice) are eligible. In active mode, ambiguous dynamic LONG items get downgraded while the eligible fallback items never do. Shadow rows and the cache-shadow share are computed on the wrong p

fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/spawn.py:1410 [med]: provider="claude" is passed only in the run_worker review and fallback-execute paths. The Codex dispatch path never passes provider="codex", and scout passes none. Codex-executed tasks therefore log cache_cost None and cache_data 'missing', and the Codex write_ratio is never used.

fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/cli.py:694 [low]: The --cache-shadow summary reads decision_log with `a.root or scorecard.STATE`, while the context card uses scorecard.STATE, so the two can describe different data. The presented level is parsed from the candidates suffix. Under active cache_mode that suffix is already the adjusted level, so changed_share reads 0 even when adjustments were applied.

fix round 1: address review T-1263 comment orchestrator/cache_telemetry.py:40 [low]: dynamic_cost indexes ratios[f"{provider}_write_ratio"] directly, so an unexpected provider string raises KeyError. route() is meant never to raise for configuration, and this would break the shadow row for that call.

fix round 1 rule: Eligibility: only the generic source_type fallback reason strings are eligible for downgrade; 'ambiguous' and every other named-rule reason are exempt (invert the current test, add a test with an ambiguous dynamic LONG item untouched and a fallback dynamic LONG item downgraded). Pass provider='codex' on the Codex dispatch path in daemon/spawn and provider='claude' for scout and the other Claude roles so no Codex run logs cache_data missing. In the --cache-shadow summary use the same root as the context card and read the presented level from the deterministic map (cache_adjusted_level versus the level stored before adjustment, stored explicitly on the row as presented_level), not from the candidates suffix. dynamic_cost returns None for an unknown provider string instead of raising.

comments.issue: The new `_choice` fallback branch returns `LONG, source_type` for test_result and worker_partial, which changes their reason from 'ambiguous'. That alters the `ambiguous` list even in shadow mode. The eligible fallback set is also only these two types. I saw only the diff hunks, so I could not confirm whether other generic fallback reasons exist.

`_cacheability` no longer treats source_type worker_partial as dynamic unless provenance is also worker_partial. A worker_partial item with other provenance is never downgraded and gets no cache cost.

scout_packet builds a `Pool()` and runs `_shadow_route` on every call when cfg is None. That logs a decision row and can raise for direct callers. run_worker wraps the call in try/except, but other callers may not.
